plan.summary:
Export the retry policy from both the TypeScript package and the Rust core crate. Library users can now import `RetryPolicy` and its options to build their own retry policy.

- `src/index.ts` re-exports `RetryPolicy` and the `RetryOptions` type from `./retry`.
- `crates/core/src/lib.rs` re-exports `retry::RetryPolicy` at the crate root.
plan.riskRationale: Two one-line re-exports widen the public API. They add no new logic. The public surface must stay stable once released.
plan.storyArc: One purpose: make the retry policy part of the public API. The TypeScript entry point and the Rust crate root each get one re-export line, so one topic covers both.

topics.title: Export RetryPolicy from the public entry points
topics.narrativeBrief: What new public API do library users get? Compare the TypeScript re-export (RetryPolicy and RetryOptions type) with the Rust re-export (RetryPolicy only). Verify that the retry modules define these names, and note that the Rust side exports no options type.
